open_questions: TECH DEBT (pre-existing, confirmed not introduced by P19B-C): quality_check.py reports src-tauri/frontend/src/components/room/Canvas.tsx at file_loc 3193 over the 2600 limit, but the iter/P19B-C/before/ snapshot proves it was already 3190 before that task (which added only the 3 lines that correctly reuse the shared Permissions renderer). Because the gate fails a whole round on any changed file over the limit, whoever next touches Canvas.tsx must split it (FilesPanel at lines ~1858-2339 and the terminal-sidebar helpers are the obvious extractable regions). DECISION NEEDED: whether to schedule a dedicated frontend refactor task, or to record a per-file exemption for this legacy file in the evidence rules.

M04 regression REPAIRED out-of-band (2026-09-28) and interactive_menu re-greened; ONE test (t35) still red pending a product call. Repaired: record_failure's run.failed payload had been reduced to {"attemptId"/"ownedAttempt"} with the reason dropped (param renamed `_error: &str`); run_manager.rs now journals the reason in all three branches, so clients/TUI receive the true failure text (TUI shows '没有已配置的默认 Provider；运行尚未启动' instead of '未知错误'); TUI failure_guidance now recognizes the pre-run Provider-guard wording so the /setup guidance survives. Verified: runtime 445/0 unchanged, r-code-tui lib 124/0, clippy/fmt clean, interactive_menu green. STILL RED: r-code-tui t35::honest_failure_lifecycle_through_shared_service. The test has drifted across >=3 layered runtime behavior changes and each fix reveals the next: (a) dropped error payload [repaired], (b) an unconfigured provider is now rejected by a pre-run Provider guard before run.started so runs台账 is empty [t35 runs-assertion updated], (c) set_preferences to a provider that is not actually configured is now refused [NEW failure at t35:204]. DECISION NEEDED (DEFERRED 2026-09-28 by user): adjudicate the current behavior for (c) (should setting a model preference for an unconfigured provider succeed or fail?) and whether t35 should be rewritten as a pre-dispatch-rejection test, or declare it a baseline. The user chose to defer the TUI triage and prioritize the app/desktop side (P19B-C); treat this 1 red t35 test as a known, accepted deferral for now. Note r-code-tui/r-code-host are workspace members but outside the house cumulative denominator, which is why this drifted unnoticed since M04.

Test hygiene on Windows: the r-code-tui suites that use tests/daemon_common spawn detached r-code-service.exe daemons that outlive the test run and keep target/debug/r-code-service.exe open, so the NEXT run's in-test `cargo build -p r-code-runtime --bin r-code-service` fails with 'failed to remove file' and every daemon_common test turns red at daemon_common/mod.rs:25 with a shifting failure set. Remedy used here: enumerate r-code-service.exe, confirm each is a test leftover by its --ipc-name/--data-root, terminate them, rebuild the binary once, then run. DECISION NEEDED: whether the TUI suites should stop their own daemons (drop-guard) so a leaked process cannot poison the next run.

P20 KEPT with an honest half-wired gate, and P21 (2026-09-28) confirmed the same shape is load-bearing: production binds neither a check native backend nor a preparation route, and current_platform_material still reports backend 'none-this-wave' + status Unsupported, so required checks are Unavailable and dependency preparation is refused on every platform rather than actually sandboxed. P21 additionally proved WHY the shell trait cannot carry this: r_code_gateway::execution_backend::CommandSpec has fields for command/cwd/timeout only, so mounts and an environment allowlist cannot reach a process at all - which is why preparation now runs through the dedicated DependencyPrepRoute trait (a route that receives the whole DependencyPrepSpec) instead of CommandExecutionBackend. DECISION NEEDED for the round that binds a real platform backend: implement DependencyPrepRoute (and the check-side equivalent) over sandbox/windows.rs build_appcontainer_launch_plan + process_supervisor SpawnSpec - Windows first, since this host executes natively - rather than widening CommandSpec, because widening it drags the bash-tool path into the blast radius. P21 also left prepare_dependencies deliberately unwired (s20 asserts zero production callers), so no user-visible fetch exists yet. P22 (2026-09-29) adds a third unwired surface and two backend seams the same round must eventually close: `ManagedProcessService` is constructed by no production path (s04/s05 pin run_manager.rs and bin/r-code-service.rs free of supervisor wiring), and `ProcessTreeBackend` has no stdin boundary, so interactive `write_validated` answers NoInputChannel for every v1 backend while honest truncation reporting needs a continuation signal in `ProcessReadReply` (r-code-harness-protocol, outside those tasks' file lists). DECISION NEEDED: whether P23+ or a dedicated round implements the input-channel + read-continuation seams.

FLAKE POLICY NEEDED for the Windows-native process identity/timing suites. Two members of the same family now fail intermittently in a full `cargo test -p r-code-runtime` run and pass in isolation: s07_windows_job_proof::supervisor_completes_windows_backend_runs_with_journal_tree_ids (pre-termination marker must survive into the stored tail; seen 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29) and t14a_contain_windows_process_trees_with_job_objects::owner_identity_uses_start_time_not_bare_pids (seen 2026-09-29 during P22). P21/P22 each added suites that spawn real children, so the load sensitivity grows with every process task. DECISION: fix the capture/identity races (bound the drain before the termination proof; avoid start-time granularity assumptions) or serialize / limit test threads for the Windows-native suites. Until then, a red member must be re-measured alone and BOTH numbers reported, and a green run must never be kept as the only evidence.

P22 shipped a live process supervisor: operation identity is now tree-{attempt}-{ownership-epoch}-{sequence} and a fenced restart legitimately produces a NEW supervised tree. Any later task that assumes tree-id shape or reuses handles across restarts must read processes.rs first. Additionally register_profile_effect only parse-checks, so a profile/effect contradiction surfaces at open, not at registration - decide whether registration should refuse earlier.

P23 WIP LIVE RED (2026-09-29, measured, not a guess): `node scripts/harness-packaging.test.mjs` fails its staged==source assertion because plugins/native/harness.json was advanced to apiMinor 3 (P23.4) while the copy that actually ships inside the desktop bundle, src-tauri/plugins/native/harness.json, is still apiMinor 2 - the exact mirror defect P19A was written up for. src-tauri/... is NOT one of P23's eight declared files, so fixing it needs a recorded deviation, and weakening the assertion is not an option. Two further unverified P23 claims block a KEEP judgement and are recorded here so nobody assumes they hold: (1) whether containment is established BEFORE the child executes - the last code I read still created the child with Command::new(..).spawn() and called prove_contained afterwards, and the repair delegation that was asked to move it to a suspended-create + job-assign + resume shape died at its turn limit, so this is unknown; (2) whether acceptance 1's 'route through supervisor' means ProcessSupervisor::start_with_write_profile as P22 did, or whether transport.rs's private SupervisedTree + IsProcessInJob/PGID proof is an equivalent substitute. Also outstanding: cross-target verification of the macOS/Linux branches (the repair agent was mid-edit on code it cannot compile on this Windows host) and the declared suite s23_harness_supervision.rs, which does not exist. DECISION NEEDED from the user only if the answer to (2) is 'must use ProcessSupervisor', because that would re-scope P23 beyond its eight files; otherwise the next round proceeds on its own judgement and records the reasoning.
